questions.q: What did the on-call engineer do before pasting the failure's log into an AI assistant?
options: Stripped the log of anything identifying, keeping only the stack trace, surrounding log lines, and the transformation spec
Pasted the raw production log, including real customer IDs, unmodified
Sent the entire source database to the assistant
Skipped drafting entirely and fixed the bug from memory
questions.explain: This applies Lesson 56's hard line: the draft happens with sanitized input, never raw production data.

questions.q: What made the AI's RCA hypothesis into an actual finding rather than just a guess?
options: The engineer queried the real source table and confirmed every pre-deploy row actually had a null discount_pct
The hypothesis sounded confident and well-organized
The assistant repeated the same hypothesis twice
The engineer trusted the hypothesis without checking anything
questions.explain: Confirmation against real data, per Lesson 58's spot-check approach, is what turns a draft into a finding.

questions.q: Where did the AI assistant genuinely save time in this scenario, per the lesson?
options: Drafting the hypothesis and drafting the one-line fix, both of which the engineer still verified
Deciding on its own that the fix was correct without any human check
Directly querying the production database on its own
Replacing the need for the engineer to look at any real data
questions.explain: The assistant sped up both drafting steps, but the engineer verified each one against real data or the actual business rule.

questions.q: Why wasn't the fix considered "done" once the pipeline ran without an error?
options: The engineer still had to confirm the output matched what the business rule actually expected, not just that the code executed
A fix is done as soon as it runs without throwing an error
The pipeline can never be tested against real failing rows
Business rules are irrelevant to whether a fix is correct
questions.explain: Running without an error and producing the actually-correct output are two different checks — the second one matters more.

questions.q: What is the throughline connecting all the steps in this worked example?
options: The AI sped up drafting at each stage, but a human decision determined what was sanitized, what was confirmed, and what actually shipped
The AI made every decision independently with no human involvement
Guardrails only applied to the RCA step, not the fix
Verification was optional since the assistant sounded confident
questions.explain: Every step that mattered — sanitizing, confirming, checking the fix — was a human decision, matching the chapter's overall throughline.
